title: Build, clean, build again
objective: Complete the Makefile with a clean target that removes everything make created, so the same three recipes can run from scratch again.
hint: clean should delete every file the other rules produce, including the generated blah.c. After it runs, make must be able to rebuild the program from nothing.

steps.description: the first build runs all three recipes
steps.stdout:
echo "int main() { return 0; }" > blah.c # Runs first
cc -c blah.c -o blah.o # Runs second
cc blah.o -o blah # Runs third

steps.description: clean leaves the directory as it found it
the same three recipes run again from a clean tree
steps.stdout:
echo "int main() { return 0; }" > blah.c # Runs first
cc -c blah.c -o blah.o # Runs second
cc blah.o -o blah # Runs third

lesson.prediction: If you build again after cleaning, which recipes will be re-executed?
hints: clean must remove all artifacts created by this set of exercises.
Build once, clean again, observe a third time.
If any files remain, make will treat them as existing targets.
lesson.explanation: After clean deletes the target, make will re-walk the entire dependency chain next time.
